[
  {
    "n": 1,
    "kind": "Example",
    "title": "Flight Punctuality Conditional Probabilities",
    "source": "Lecture 1",
    "statement": "The probability that a regularly scheduled flight departs on time is $P(D) = 0.83$, arrives on time is $P(A) = 0.82$, and both departs and arrives on time is $P(D \\cap A) = 0.78$. Find the probability that a plane (a) arrives on time, given that it departed on time, and (b) departed on time, given that it has arrived on time."
  },
  {
    "n": 2,
    "kind": "Example",
    "title": "Biased Die Perfect Square Roll",
    "source": "Lecture 1",
    "statement": "Consider the event $B$ of rolling a perfect square on a die where even numbers are twice as likely as odd numbers, giving $P(B) = 1/3$. Given the additional knowledge that the toss resulted in a number greater than 3, evaluate the conditional probability $P(B|A)$ over the reduced sample space."
  },
  {
    "n": 3,
    "kind": "Example",
    "title": "Fair Die Outcome Independence",
    "source": "Lecture 1",
    "statement": "Consider rolling a single fair six-sided die with sample space $S = \\{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6\\}$. Determine whether Event $A$ (rolling an even number) and Event $B$ (rolling a multiple of 3) are independent events."
  },
  {
    "n": 4,
    "kind": "Example",
    "title": "Defective Fuse Selection Without Replacement",
    "source": "Lecture 1",
    "statement": "A fuse box contains 20 fuses, of which 5 are defective. If 2 fuses are selected at random and removed from the box in succession without replacing the first, find the probability that both fuses are defective."
  },
  {
    "n": 5,
    "kind": "Example",
    "title": "Two-Bag Sequential Ball Draw",
    "source": "Lecture 1",
    "statement": "One bag contains 4 white balls and 3 black balls, and a second bag contains 3 white balls and 5 black balls. One ball is drawn from the first bag and placed unseen into the second bag; find the probability that a ball now drawn from the second bag is black."
  },
  {
    "n": 6,
    "kind": "Example",
    "title": "Emergency Services Joint Availability",
    "source": "Lecture 1",
    "statement": "A small town has one fire engine and one ambulance with availability probabilities of $0.98$ and $0.92$, respectively. Assuming they operate independently, find the probability that both vehicles will be available in an emergency resulting from a burning building."
  },
  {
    "n": 7,
    "kind": "Example",
    "title": "Successive Card Draws Without Replacement",
    "source": "Lecture 1",
    "statement": "Three cards are drawn in succession without replacement from an ordinary deck of playing cards. Find the probability that the first card is a red ace, the second card is a 10 or a jack, and the third card is greater than 3 but less than 7."
  },
  {
    "n": 8,
    "kind": "Example",
    "title": "Urn Sampling Red Ball Count",
    "source": "Lecture 1",
    "statement": "Two balls are drawn in succession without replacement from an urn containing 4 red balls and 3 black balls. List the possible outcomes in the sample space and assign the corresponding numerical values of the random variable $Y$ representing the number of red balls."
  },
  {
    "n": 9,
    "kind": "Example",
    "title": "Production Line Component Defect Indicator",
    "source": "Lecture 1",
    "statement": "Components arriving from a production line are inspected as defective or not defective. Define an indicator random variable $X$ taking the value 1 if the component is defective and 0 if it is not defective."
  },
  {
    "n": 10,
    "kind": "Example",
    "title": "Radioactive Particle Decay Continuous Space",
    "source": "Lecture 1",
    "statement": "Define the sample space for measuring the exact time in seconds until a radioactive particle decays. Determine the structure of this sample space $S = [0, \\infty) \\subset \\mathbb{R}$ as a continuous sample space."
  },
  {
    "n": 11,
    "kind": "Example",
    "title": "Purchased Laptop Defectives Distribution",
    "source": "Lecture 1",
    "statement": "A shipment of 20 laptop computers contains 3 defective units. If a school purchases 2 of these computers at random, determine the probability distribution function and the cumulative distribution function for the number of defective units."
  }
]
